claim: An employer's failure to investigate internal complaints of ethnic harassment within a reasonable timeframe constitutes constructive notice of a hostile work environment. The Fifth Circuit held that managerial inaction lasting more than sixty days following a documented complaint is sufficient to establish employer liability under Title VII.
citation: Bustamante v. Kelso Paper & Packaging Corp., 78 F.3d 541 (5th Cir. 1996)
initial_reasoning: The citation to Bustamante v. Kelso Paper & Packaging Corp. supports the claim that an employer's failure to investigate internal complaints of ethnic harassment within a reasonable timeframe can constitute constructive notice of a hostile work environment, as the Fifth Circuit's decision in this case establishes a precedent for employer liability under Title VII in such scenarios, specifically addressing the timeframe for managerial action. The court's ruling implies that inaction beyond a certain period, such as sixty days, can be sufficient to establish liability. This aligns with the principles of Title VII, which mandates employers to take prompt and effective action against harassment.
